message: No detected input validation: The code extracts fields from the incoming JSON payload and passes them directly to the model without any schema validation, type checks, or value-range guards.
No detected untrusted source handling: The training data is fetched from a raw GitHub URL via pd.read_csv with no checksum verification, authentication, or pinned commit/revision to ensure integrity.
No detected label flipping detection: No label distribution checks, validation against expected label sets, or label-noise detection tools are applied before or during training.

No detected data poisoning defenses: The preparation code uses only mean imputation and standard scaling with no outlier detection, statistical anomaly checks, or filtering of suspicious training samples.

No detected model integrity verification: The load_model() function loads the model directly via joblib.load() from a local path with no hash check, signature verification, or pinned revision to verify integrity.

No detected label distribution validation: The retrain() function loads data and trains directly without any class balance check, expected-label-set verification, or anomalous sample detection on the labels.
No detected backdoor or trigger detection: There is no trigger detection, activation-pattern analysis, or gradient anomaly detection anywhere in the training pipeline.
No detected differential privacy: The code uses a standard XGBClassifier with no differential privacy library (Opacus, TensorFlow Privacy, DP-SGD, etc.) applied.
No detected adversarial robustness testing: No adversarial robustness testing libraries (Foolbox, ART, FGSM, PGD) or stress tests are present anywhere in the code.

No detected metric tampering protection: The retrain() function evaluates ROC-AUC on the same training data used to fit the model (no held-out test set, no data hashing, no independent metrics), providing no protection against metric manipulation.

No detected input sanitization: The inference path passes raw JSON payload and URL-parsed profile directly to predict() without any schema validation, shape checks, range validation, or rejection of malformed/missing fields.

No detected output bounds checks: The predict() function and human_readable_payload() perform no sanity checks on the model's output probability (e.g., verifying it is within [0,1] or guarding against NaN values) before returning it.
No detected prompt injection defenses: This is not an LLM-based pipeline; it uses an XGBoost classifier on tabular credit data, so prompt injection defenses are not applicable.
